briefdescription.para: HEALTH_n flags bits — node-level health conditions (maps to NodeHealthPayload.flags).
HEALTH_n faultId dictionary (#163) — cross-node fault codes.

detaileddescription.para: Coarse, one active at a time on the wire; the exact device is logged locally on DiagSerial, not the frame. The client maps id → human label (SkyHawkClient#40). Each node type contributes the codes relevant to its fault sources; append as new sources appear.

briefdescription.para: TELEM_n page ids (#216) — byte 0 of TelemPayload, naming the layout of bytes 1-7.

detaileddescription.para: Global and append-only: a page id means the same layout whichever node sends it, so the client decodes by page, not by node type. 0x00 is invalid. Layouts (little-endian): PDU_RAIL_12V / PDU_RAIL_5V: [1] PduRailFlag bits · [2-3] vAvgMv u16 · [4-5] vMinMv u16 · [6-7] iAvgMa int16 PDU_STATUS: [1] PduStatusFlag bits · [2-3] ntcTempDC int16 (0.1 °C, INT16_MIN = unavailable) · [4-5] i12PeakMa u16 · [6-7] i5PeakMa u16

briefdescription.para: PDU_RAIL_* page byte 1 — per-rail condition bits (all zero = healthy).
PDU_STATUS page byte 1 — board condition bits (all zero = healthy, calibrated).
Neutral node-status contract for every OpenSkyhawk node (PanelGroup, PanelBridge, PDU).

detaileddescription.para: This is the neutral home for node-status vocabulary so it isn't shaped around any one node flavour (PanelGroup/OutputBase) or the HID namespace. NodeHealthPayload (the CAN HEALTH_n frame struct) stays in CANProtocol.h; the fault detail strings stay local (DiagSerial), never on the wire. Header-only contract + a tiny FaultSource registry (NodeStatus.cpp).
